name: result-codec-and-framecodec-ride
currentState: A C# engine-separation PREP feature (roadmap state: refined; no spec, no code). Scope: a net-new result-envelope codec that serializes the engine's execution result (status / bindings / var-name→writer map / suspended-goal detail / captured output / errors, incl. an unbound-variable encoding) into a self-contained byte chunk that crosses a process boundary, riding the shipped 025 FrameCodec frame envelope + TcpTransport, with a payload-type discriminator. It exists only to put execution results on a wire between a SEPARATED engine process and a REPL/client process. Roadmap drift vs the chosen baseline: it presupposes the REPL/engine cross-process split, which the chosen approach's M1 explicitly REJECTS (M1 is in-process, REPL calls the engine as a typed Gleam value with no wire). The reconciliation memo also flags two corrections: the dossier's "distinguish by FrameCodec Kind byte" is wrong — OffKind=1 is the Whole/Fragment discriminant, the payload-type byte must live INSIDE the chunk; and ExecutionResult today carries only Status/Bindings/Error (the var-writer map, SuspendedGoals/BlockingReaders, and output are all leaked/dropped, to be supplied by its deps #11/#10).
contribution: Two separable parts with different fates. (1) The FrameCodec frame-envelope byte-parity (version byte, 22-byte big-endian header, CRC-32, MTU fragmentation/reassembly, 64 MiB guard) IS load-bearing for M2 cross-runtime — it folds into #36 (link-layer) step 5a as a sub-requirement: a Gleam FrameCodec must match the C# envelope byte-for-byte ALONGSIDE the TLV term format, both required for the cross-runtime gate (Approach 2's uniquely load-bearing insight, re-instated against Approach 3's drop). (2) The result-envelope-on-wire codec itself is OFF the M1/M2 faithful-semantics path: M1 is in-process so no result codec is needed; the envelope FIELD-SET (status/bindings/var→writer/suspended/output/errors) is already absorbed as the engine's typed Gleam return type via #11+#10 folding into #6. Serializing that return type only matters if a cross-process REPL seam is later wanted (post-baseline, non-blocking).
faithfulnessRole: The frame-envelope parity serves M2 wire-faithfulness: byte-identical FrameCodec framing is half of the SC-001 byte-identical-split gate and the FR-031 identical-cross-runtime-verdict gate (the TLV term format is the other half). The result-envelope codec's only faithfulness relevance is latent/deferred — it would have to faithfully transmit the three-valued status (Success/Suspend/Fail as distinct codes, never conflating Fail and Suspend) and suspended-goal/blocking-reader detail across a process boundary without leaking a live heap address (the same deep-resolve obligation that is fatal for both C# VarRefs and Gleam immutable heap addrs). But in the in-process M1 there is no boundary, so that role does not activate on the baseline path.
improvement: Split and dissolve the feature; do not specify it standalone. (1) Re-target the FrameCodec frame-envelope byte-parity into #36's spec (step 5a): implement a Gleam-native FrameCodec (raw big-endian header, CRC-32, fragmentation) validated against the shipped C# FrameCodec as the byte-parity oracle — keep-cross-runtime validation, not a port-now obligation. Drop the C#-specific OffKind correction and the Dart-mirror byte-parity obligation (U2) as no longer relevant. (2) Defer the result-envelope-on-wire codec post-baseline under #030; if a cross-process REPL seam ever materializes, re-express it Gleam-native over the engine's already-existing typed return type (from #11/#10→#6), encoding distinct status codes + an unbound-var sentinel + deep-resolved ground terms — no need to design it now. Discard the C# substrate specifics (PayloadSerializer tag reuse, payload-type-prefix-byte choice) — they are C# artifacts, not Gleam design inputs.
rationale: The chosen approach's disposition table is explicit and unambiguous for this id: "fold-into-gleam (#36) — frame-envelope parity becomes a #36 sub-req (re-instated vs Approach 3's drop); envelope-on-wire = realign(defer)", and Step 0 says "fold #15 frame-envelope + #29 into #36's spec" while the ordering lists "#15 result-envelope-on-wire (only if a cross-process REPL seam is wanted)" as post-baseline non-blocking. As a standalone feature it is out-of-path: its primary purpose (wire serialization of execution results for a cross-process REPL/engine split) is precisely what M1 in-process design eliminates, and the only durably useful piece — frame-envelope byte-parity — is M2 work that belongs inside #36, not a separate feature. Hence recommendedOrder 0 (folded/deferred), milestone M2 via #36, not itself a critical milestone. The reconciliation memo independently confirms the C# nature, the net-new status, and the FrameCodec facts, all verified in source.

name: repl-engine-process-split-mvp
currentState: A C#/.NET MVP that splits the REPL into two OS processes — a thin REPL client and a GLP engine host — talking over a TCP-loopback FrameCodec: the client sends SOURCE TEXT (compiler stays engine-side), the engine returns a structured result envelope; one engine / one client; C# one-accept listener; bootstrap from self.glp (memo:39-43). Dossier kind = MVP; "smallest end-to-end split." Roadmap status: captured/refined, WSJF=3.25 RICE=4500 effort=L (memo:45) — NOT specified, NOT built. contribution: Contributes nothing to M1/M2 faithfulness. Its deliverable is a pure OPERATIONAL mechanism — an OS process boundary plus a TCP-loopback transport and one-accept host listener (csharp/glp_link/transports/TcpTransport.cs:40-49; FrameCodec.cs:7-13). The chosen approach makes M1 explicitly IN-PROCESS: M1 is "a single combined GLP instance, as in Dart and C#," both of which run engine+front-end in one process; importing the engine-separation split into M1 is rejected because it "adds a message-copy/heap-index-leak hazard and buys zero execution-semantics fidelity." For M2, the analogous concurrency (per-link process pairs, supervision, multi-accept, mailboxes, per-link FIFO) is exactly what BEAM/AtomVM provide natively via raw erlang:spawn + Subjects — process-split is named in the chosen approach as the canonical supersede-by-BEAM operational layer. The only faithfulness-relevant ideas this feature touched (result-envelope field-set, server-side deep-resolve so no live heap addr escapes the boundary, frame envelope) are NOT owned here — they are re-homed: #11+#10 fold-into-gleam(#6) and #15 fold-into-gleam(#36). What remains in #13 is just the C# wiring/process plumbing, which is off-path.
faithfulnessRole: None as a feature. The boundary-deref discipline it relied on (the engine resolves to ground/self-contained snapshots so no live heap address crosses, _ResolveDeepForTrace at glp_engine.cs:607-619) IS a real faithfulness concern (deref correctness PC-7/PC-8, no leaked heap addrs — equally fatal for Gleam's immutable heap addrs), but that role is discharged by #11 (result-envelope-and-deep-resolve, fold-into-gleam) and the engine's own result producer, not by this process-split feature.

Preserve only its concept fragments where they already live: (a) the result-envelope field-set + server-side deep-resolve as the engine's typed return value — already folded into the Gleam REPL #6 via #11/#10; (b) the FrameCodec frame envelope as a parity sub-req of the Gleam link layer #36 via #15. rationale: The chosen approach names this feature by id with an explicit disposition and rationale, so the verdict is direct, not inferred.
